observations: Three photos show a used automatic transmission assembly in a workshop or scrapyard setting.
The unit has a silver-colored metal casing with visible wear, dirt, and some rust.
A black plastic cover is attached to the front, likely for the torque converter or fluid reservoir.
There is a white label on the front cover with a barcode and some text, but the text is too small to read clearly.
A black hose with '1/2"' and 'SPE' markings is connected to the top of the unit.
The background shows other engine parts, suggesting a used parts market environment.
No visible branding or model numbers are readable on the unit itself.
The seller claims it is an 'American Drive Gearbox Ford Fusion' and '4 cylinder'.

claims.evidence: No visible branding or model identifiers on the gearbox in any photo. The seller's text is not proof.
No engine or cylinder count visible in photos. Cannot be confirmed from images alone.

claims.claim: Tokunbo, direct from Belgium. Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The gearbox may not be from a Ford Fusion or may not be a 4-cylinder unit as claimed.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine or transmission label showing the model number or VIN, or a photo of the engine bay with the correct model badge.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic used automatic transmission, not as a specific Ford Fusion 4-cylinder unit.

risks.risk: The gearbox may be damaged or non-functional.
risks.proof: A video or photo showing the internal components (e.g., gears, solenoids, fluid lines) or a test run if possible.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working or with unknown functionality.

risks.risk: The gearbox may have been salvaged from a wrecked or accident-damaged vehicle.
risks.proof: A photo of the vehicle's VIN plate or a clear shot of the engine bay showing the original vehicle's condition.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a used unit with unknown history.

proof_requests: Close-up of the engine or gearbox code: the plate, sticker or number stamped on the block or case.
Clear photo of the label on the front cover showing the model or part number.
Photo of the engine bay or VIN plate to confirm the vehicle's make and model.
Video or photo showing the internal components or a test run if possible.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
